title: Giustizia minorile e competenze interculturali
summary: In today’s societies, increasingly shaped by pluralism and multiculturalism, the juvenile justice system is called upon to engage with new challenges—extending beyond institutional frameworks to include relational and educational dimensions. When the life paths of young people with a migratory background intersect with the justice system, complex questions emerge around the meeting of rights and cultures, approaches to difference, and the competences of those who work within it. Based on empirical research conducted within the Italian juvenile justice system, this volume explores the intercultural competences of its professionals—magistrates, honorary judges of the juvenile court (non-career judges appointed for their social and educational expertise), lawyers and other practitioners—focusing on how these are developed, interpreted and enacted in everyday practice. These competences concern every encounter, as diversity is not an exception but a constitutive condition of human relationships. From this perspective, juvenile justice is seen not only as a legal domain, but also as an educational space in which professionals cultivate knowledge, skills and practices that enable them to engage with people in all their complexity. Building on these insights, the book outlines a profile of the intercultural practitioner in juvenile justice system, identifying key dimensions and areas for further development. It also offers valuable reflections for training and professional development, contributing to more equitable and critically informed practices. This volume is aimed at scholars and researchers in the field of education, professionals working in juvenile justice and socio-educational services, and university students interested in intercultural competences within professional contexts.
